members.local_label: Section 2.1 — target bandit and reward functions
members.source_heading: Section 2.1 — target bandit and reward functions
members.statement_original:
Let $Q$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}\times[0,1]^{K}$ that generates a sequence of independent random vectors $(X^{Q},Y^{Q,(1)},\cdots,Y^{Q,(K)})$. At each time point $t$, based on the covariate $X_{t}^{Q}\in\mathcal{X}$ drawn from the marginal distribution $Q_{X}$, a decision-maker selects an arm $k\in[K]$ and receives a random reward $Y_{t}^{Q,(k)}\in[0,1]$ associated with the chosen arm according to the conditional distribution $Q_{Y^{(k)}| X_{t}^{Q}}$. We assume that for any $k\in[K]$ and $t\geq1$, the random reward $Y_{t}^{Q,(k)}$ is a random variable with conditional expectation given by 
\[
\mathbb{E}\big[Y_{t}^{Q,(k)}\,|\,X_{t}^{Q}\big]=f_{k}^{Q}(X_{t}^{Q}),
\]
 where $f_{k}^{Q}:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow[0,1]$ is an unknown function called a reward function. A policy $\pi$ is a collection of functions $\{\pi_{t}\}_{t\geq1}$ where $\pi_{t}: \mathcal{X}\rightarrow[K]$ prescribe the arm to pull at time $t$.

members.statement_original:
In the context of transfer learning, we assume that the decision-maker is given a batch dataset $\mathcal{D}^{P} \coloneqq \{(X_{i}^{P},\pi_{i}^{P}, Y_{i}^{P,(\pi_{i}^{P})})\}_{i=1}^{n_{P}}$. This dataset is collected from a contextual $K$-armed bandit over $n_{P}$ rounds, of which the underlying probability distribution $P$ generates a sequence of independent random vectors $(X^{P},Y^{P,(1)},\cdots,Y^{P,(K)})\in\mathcal{X}\times[0,1]^{K}$. Here, $X_{i}^{P}\in\mathcal{X}$ represents the covariate observed at time $i$, policy $\pi_{i}^{P}:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow[K]$ denotes the selected arm at time $i$, and $Y_{i}^{P,(\pi_{i}^{P})}$ corresponds to the observed random reward at time $i$. Similar to the $Q$-bandit, it is assumed that for any $k\in[K]$ and $i\geq1$, the random reward $Y_{i}^{P,(k)}$ of the $P$-bandit obeys 
\[
\mathbb{E}\big[Y_{i}^{P,(k)}\,|\,X_{i}^{P}\big]=f_{k}^{P}(X_{i}^{P}),
\]
 for an unknown function $f_{k}^{P}:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow[0,1]$. Throughout the paper, we denote $n \coloneqq n_{Q} \vee n_{P}$.

As mentioned in the introduction, this paper focuses on the covariate shift model. To be specific, it is assumed that the marginal distributions of covariates in the $P$-bandit and $Q$-bandit are different (i.e. $P_{X} \neq Q_{X}$) while the distributions of rewards conditioned on the covariate value are identical (i.e. $P_{Y^{(k)}|X}=Q_{Y^{(k)}|X}$ for all $1\leq k\leq K$). In particular, the latter implies that the reward functions of the two bandits are also identical. We denote these common reward functions as $f_{k}(x)\coloneqq f_{k}^{P}(x)\equiv f_{k}^{Q}(x)$ for all $k\in[K]$ and $x\in\mathcal{X}$.

members.local_label: Section 2.1 — oracle policy and expected regret, equation (2)
members.source_heading: Section 2.1 — oracle policy and expected regret, equation (2)
members.statement_original:
Recall that $\pi^{\star}$ is the oracle policy with access to full knowledge of the reward functions $\{f_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}$. It is straightforward to see that given a covariate value $x$, the oracle policy $\pi^{\star}$ selects any arm with the largest expected reward, with ties broken arbitrarily. In other words, 
\[
\pi^{\star}(x)\in\mathop{\mathrm{argmax}}_{k\in[K]}f_{k}(x).
\]
 Therefore, for any policy $\pi=\{\pi_{t}\}_{t\geq1}$, the regret of $\pi$ in the $Q$-bandit defined in (1) has the following expression: 
\[
\begin{aligned}\mathbb{E}[R_{n_Q}(\pi)] & =\mathbb{E}\bigg[ \sum_{t=1}^{n_{Q}} \Big( f_{\pi^{\star}(X_t^Q)}(X_{t}^{Q})-f_{\pi_{t}(X_t^Q)}(X_{t}^{Q}) \Big) \bigg]  \\
& =\mathbb{E}\bigg[ \sum_{t=1}^{n_{Q}} \Big( \max_{k\in[K]} f_{k}(X_{t}^{Q})-f_{\pi_{t}(X_t^Q)}(X_{t}^{Q}) \Big)\bigg].\end{aligned}\tag{2}
\]
 In the remainder of the paper, we may drop the subscript $n_Q$ whenever there is no confusion.

members.statement_original:
The reward functions $\{f_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}$ are $\left(\beta,C_{\beta}\right)$-Hölder continuous for some constants $0<\beta\leq1,C_{\beta}>0$, i.e. for any $k\in[K]$, 
\[
\big|f_{k}(x)-f_{k}(x')\big|\leq C_{\beta} \| x-x'\|_{\infty}^{\beta},\quad\forall x,x'\in\mathcal{X}.
\]

members.local_label: Section 2.2 — pointwise maximum and second pointwise maximum
members.source_heading: Section 2.2 — pointwise maximum and second pointwise maximum
members.statement_original:
Next, it is natural to expect that the gap between the reward functions is a pivotal measure of a contextual multi-armed bandit problem's complexity. To this end, let $f_{(1)}$ (resp. $f_{(2)}$) denote the pointwise maximum (resp. the second pointwise maximum) of the reward functions $\{f_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}$, namely 
\[
f_{(1)}(x)  \coloneqq\max_{k\in[K]}f_{k}(x),
\]
 and 
\[
f_{(2)}(x)\coloneqq\begin{cases}
\max\limits_{k\in[K]}\big\{ f_{k}(x):f_{k}(x)<f_{(1)}(x)\big\}, & \text{if }\min\limits_{k\in[K]}f_{k}(x)\neq\max\limits_{k\in[K]}f_{k}(x),\\
f_{(1)}(x), & \text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\]

members.statement_original:
There exist constants $\alpha\geq0,C_{\alpha}>0$ such that the reward functions $\{f_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K}$ and marginal distribution $Q_{X}$ satisfy 
\[
Q_X\big(0<f_{(1)}(X)-f_{(2)}(X)\leq\delta\big)\leq C_{\alpha}\delta^{\alpha},\quad\forall0<\delta\leq1.
\]
There exist constants $\overline{q}>\underline{q}>0$ such that $\underline{q} r^d \leq Q_{X}(B(x,r)) \leq \overline{q} r^d$ for any $x\in \mathsf{supp}(Q_{X})$ and $r\in(0,1]$.

In addition, the covariate-arm pairs $\big\{\big(X^{P}_{i}, \pi_{i}^{P}\big)\big\}_{i=1}^{n_P}$ in the pre-collected source dataset are assumed to be generated i.i.d. according to $X^{P}_{i} \sim P_{X}$ and $\pi_{i}^{P}(X^{P}_{i}) \sim \mu(\cdot \, | \, X^{P}_{i})$, where $\{\mu(\cdot \, | \, x) \}_{x\in \mathcal{X}}$ is a collection of probability distributions over the arm set $[K]$.

Define the transfer exponent $\gamma \in \mathbb{R}_{+} \cup \{0,\infty\}$ of $P_{X}$ with respect to $Q_{X}$ to be the smallest constant such that 
\[
P_{X}(B(x, r)) \geq c_{\gamma}r^{\gamma} Q_{X}(B(x, r)),\quad\forall x\in\mathsf{supp}(Q_{X}), r \in (0, 1],
\]
 for some constant $0 < c_{\gamma} \leq 1$.

Define the exploration coefficient $\kappa  \in [0, 1]$ of a collection of distributions over the arm set $\{\mu(\cdot \, | \, x) \}_{x\in\mathcal{X}}$ with respect to $Q_X$ as 
\[
\kappa  \coloneqq\inf_{\substack{k\in [K],\,x\in \mathsf{supp}(Q_{X})}} K \mu(k \, | \, x).
\]

Finally, we assume the number of arms $K$ is constant throughout this paper.

Denote by $\Pi(K,\beta,C_{\beta},\alpha,C_{\alpha},\underline{q},\overline{q},\gamma,c_{\gamma}, \kappa )$ the class of nonparametric contextual $K$-armed bandits that satisfy Assumptions 1--3 and Definitions 1--2. Here and throughout the paper, we may use the shorthands $\Pi(K,\beta,\alpha,\gamma, \kappa )$ and $\Pi$ if there is no confusion.

members.statement_original:
Here, for any non-negative integer $l \geq 0$, we define a collection of bins $\mathcal{B}_{l}\coloneqq\{B_{\mathsf k}\}_{\mathsf{k} \in [2^l]^d}$ where 
\[
B_{\mathsf{k}}\coloneqq\{x\in\mathcal{X}:(k_{i}-1)2^{-l}\leq x_{i}\leq k_{i}2^{-l},\,k_{i}\in[2^{l}],\,i\in[d]\},\quad\forall\mathsf{k}=(k_{1},\dots,k_{d}).\tag{5}
\]
 Throughout the paper, we use $|B|$ to denote the side length of any bin $B$, i.e. $|B|=2^{-l}$ for any $B\in\mathcal{B}_{l}$.

members.statement_original: First, for any $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and $t \geq 1$, let $B_{t}(x)\in\mathcal{L}_{t}$ denote the bin in the partition $\mathcal{L}_{t}$ at time $t$ such that $x\in B_{t}(x)$. If there are multiple bins, we choose $B_{t}(x)$ to be the one whose center is closest to the origin. Next, for any bin $B$ and time $t \geq 1$, denote by $N_{t}(B)$ the number of times the covariate fell into $B$ prior to time $t$, i.e. $N_{t}(B)\coloneqq\sum_{1\leq s\leq t}\mathbb{1}\{X_{s}^Q\in B\}$. With these definitions in place, the policy $\pi = \{\pi_{t}\}_{t \geq 1}$ yielded by Algorithm 1 can be described by $\pi_{t} = \widetilde{\pi}_{N_{t}(B)}(B)$ with $B = B_{t}(X_t^Q)$ for any time $t \geq 1$.

members.local_label: Section 3.1 — perfect tree and child bins
members.source_heading: Section 3.1 — perfect tree and child bins
members.statement_original:
To this end, denote by $\mathcal{T}^{(l)}$ the perfect tree with root node $\mathcal{X}$ and depth $l \geq 0$, where there are $2^{i d}$ nodes in each depth $0 \leq i < l$ and each node $B$ represents a bin in set $\mathcal{B}_{i}$. The set of children of any bin $B \in \mathcal{B}_{i}$ with $i \geq 0$ is defined as $\mathsf{child}(B) \coloneqq\{ B' \in \mathcal{B}_{i + 1} : B' \subset B \}$. Then at each time $t$, the partition $\mathcal{L}_t$ induced by Algorithm 1 can be described as a set of leaf nodes of a subtree of $\mathcal{T}^{(l)}$ for some $l>0$.

Throughout the paper, the terms bin and node are used interchangeably.

members.statement_original:
Next, given a subset $\mathcal{D}$ of the source dataset $\mathcal{D}^{P}$, for any bin $B$ and arm $k$, let $n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})$ denote the number of samples in dataset $\mathcal{D}$ such that the covariate falls in bin $B$ and arm $k$ is pulled, i.e. 
\[
n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})  \coloneqq\sum_{(X_{i},\pi_{i},Y_{i})\in\mathcal{D}}\mathbb{1}\{X_{i}\in B,\,\pi_{i}=k\}.\tag{7}
\]

members.variant_note: The source summand prints Y rather than Y_i. The indexed record and the unindexed summand are both preserved.

members.statement_original:
In addition, for any non-negative integer $\tau \geq 0$, bin $B$ and arm $k$, let us define 
\[
U_{k}(\tau,B;\mathcal{D})\coloneqq
\begin{cases}
2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\tau+n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})}\log^{+}(\frac{n_{Q}|B|^{d}}{\tau})} \vee 2C_{\beta}|B|^{\beta}, & \text{if } \tau > 0, \\
2\sqrt{\frac{2}{n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})}\log^{+}(n_{Q}|B|^{d+2\beta}\vee\kappa n_{P}|B|^{d+2\beta+\gamma})} \vee 2C_{\beta}|B|^{\beta}, & \text{if } \tau = 0,
\end{cases}\tag{9}
\]
 where we recall the notation $\log^{+}(x)\coloneqq\log(x)\vee1$ and use the convention $1/0 = \infty$. The $U_{k}(\tau,B;\mathcal{D})$ can be essentially viewed as a confidence bound that quantifies the uncertainty of the reward function estimator used in Algorithm 1.

members.statement_original:
In order to achieve such an adaptive partition, for each bin $B$ and arm $k$, we assign a non-negative upper bound on the number of pulls, given by 
\[
\tau^\star_k(B;\mathcal{D}) \coloneqq\min_{\tau \in \{0\}\cup\mathbb{N}}\big\{ \tau : U_{k}(\tau,B;\mathcal{D}) 

\leq 2C_{\beta}|B|^{\beta}\big\},\tag{10}
\]
 where we recall the definition of $U_{k}(\tau,B;\mathcal{D})$ in (9).

members.local_label: Procedure 1 — Successive elimination procedure for a static bandit with source data
members.source_heading: Procedure 1 — Successive elimination procedure for a static bandit with source data
members.statement_original:
- **1.** **Input:** bin $B$, arm set $\mathcal{I}$, confidence bound function $U$, source data $\mathcal{D}$.
- **2.** Set $n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D}),\overline{Y}_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D}),\tau_{k}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D})$ as in (7), (8), (10), respectively, $\forall k\in\mathcal{I}$.
- **3.** Set $n_{k}^{P} \gets n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})$, $\overline{Y}_{k} \gets \overline{Y}_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})$, and $\tau_{k}^{\star} \gets \tau_{k}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}), \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$.
- **4.** Initialize $t\gets0$.
- **5.** Initialize $\tau_{k} \gets 0, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$. ▷ initialize pull counts
- **6.** Initialize $\underline{Y}^{\star}\gets\max\limits_{k\in\mathcal{I}}\big\{\overline{Y}_{k}-U_{k}(0,B;\mathcal{D})\big\}$. ▷ initialize largest reward lower bound
- **7.** loop
    - **8.** if $\tau_{k}\geq\tau_{k}^{\star}, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$ then ▷ condition to stop exploration
        - **9.** Set $t \gets t+1$.
        - **10.** Select arm $\widetilde{\pi}_{t}\gets\mathop{\mathrm{argmax}}\limits_{k\in\mathcal{I}}\overline{Y}_{k}$ (with ties broken arbitrarily) and receive reward $Y^{Q,({\widetilde{\pi}_{t}})}$.
        - **11.** Set $\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\gets\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}} + 1$. ▷ update pull count
        - **12.** Set $\tau_{t,k}\gets \tau_{k}, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$, and $\mathcal{I}_{t}\gets\mathcal{I}$. ▷ record pull count and active arm set
        - **13.** Set $\overline{Y}_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\gets\frac{1}{n_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}^{P}+\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}}\big(Y^{Q,({\widetilde{\pi}_{t}})}+(n_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}^{P}+\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}-1)\overline{Y}_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\big)$. ▷ update estimated reward
    - **14.** else
        - **15.** for $k\in\mathcal{I} \text{ such that } \tau_{k}<\tau_{k}^{\star}$ do ▷ only explore arms s.t. pull counts less than upper bounds
            - **16.** if $\overline{Y}_{k}+  U_{k}(\tau_{k},B;\mathcal{D}) \geq\underline{Y}^{\star}$ then ▷ eliminate arm s.t. reward upper bound is smaller than largest reward lower bound
                - **17.** Set $t \gets t+1$.
                - **18.** Select arm $\widetilde{\pi}_{t}\gets k$ and receive reward $Y^{Q,({\widetilde{\pi}_{t}})}$.
                - **19.** Set $\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\gets\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}} + 1$. ▷ update pull count
                - **20.** Set $\tau_{t,k}\gets \tau_{k}, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$, and $\mathcal{I}_{t}\gets\mathcal{I}$. ▷ record pull count and active arm set
                - **21.** Set $\overline{Y}_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\gets\frac{1}{n_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}^{P}+\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}}\big(Y^{Q,({\widetilde{\pi}_{t}})}+(n_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}^{P}+\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}-1)\overline{Y}_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\big)$. ▷ update estimated reward
                - **22.** Set $\underline{Y}^{\star}\gets\max_{k\in\mathcal{I}}\big\{\overline{Y}_{k}-U_{k}(\tau_{k},B;\mathcal{D})\big\}$. ▷ update largest reward lower bound
            - **23.** else
                - **24.** Eliminate arm $k$ from active arm set: $\mathcal{I} \gets\mathcal{I}\setminus\{k\}$.
- **25.** **Output:** policy $\{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}\}_{t\geq1}$, arm pull counts $\{(\tau_{t,k})_{k\in\mathcal{I}_t}\}_{t\geq1}$, sets of active arms $\{\mathcal{I}_{t}\}_{t\geq1}$.

members.source_heading: Algorithm 1 — Transfer learning algorithm for contextual multi-armed bandits
members.statement_original:
- **1.** **Input:** arm set $\mathcal{I}$, horizon length $n_{Q}$, smoothness parameters $\beta, C_{\beta}$, transfer parameters $\gamma$, exploration coefficient $\kappa$, $P$-data $\mathcal{D}^{P}$.
- **2.** Initialize $\mathcal{L}_{1}\gets\{\mathcal{X}\}$, $\mathcal{I}(\mathcal{X})\gets\mathcal{I}$. ▷ initialize partition and arm set
- **3.** Initialize the policy $\widetilde{\pi}(\mathcal{X})$ by Procedure 1$\big(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{I}(\mathcal{X}),U,\mathcal{D}^{P} \big)$.
- **4.** Initialize $N(\mathcal{X})\gets0$. ▷ initialize time for policy $\widetilde{\pi}(\mathcal{X})$
- **5.** Initialize $\tau_{k}(\mathcal{X}) \gets 0$, and $\tau_{k}^{\star}(\mathcal{X};\mathcal{D}^{P})$ as in (10), $\forall k\in \mathcal{I}(\mathcal{X})$. ▷ initialize rounds and set round upper bounds
- **6.** for $t=1,\dots,n_{Q}$ do
    - **7.** Draw a sample $X_{t}^{Q} \sim Q_{X}$.
    - **8.** Find the bin $B\in\mathcal{L}_{t}$ such that $X_{t}^{Q}\in B$.
    - **9.** while $|\mathcal{I}(B)|>1$
      
      and $\tau_{k}(B)\geq\tau_{k}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}), \forall k\in\mathcal{I}(B)$ do ▷ keep partitioning $B$ until reaching suitable scale
        - **10.** if $\tau_{k}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}) = 0, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}(B)$ then ▷ no exploration needed in $B$: discard suboptimal arms
            - **11.** Set $\underline{Y}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}^{P})\gets\max\limits_{k\in\mathcal{I}(B)}\big\{\overline{Y}_{k}^P(B;\mathcal{D}^{P})-  U_{k}(0,B;\mathcal{D}^{P}) \big\}$. ▷ set largest reward lower bound
            - **12.** Set $\mathcal{I}(B) \gets \big\{ k \in \mathcal{I}(B) : \overline{Y}_k^P(B;\mathcal{D}^{P})+U_{k}(0,B;\mathcal{D}^{P}) \geq \underline{Y}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}) \big\}$. ▷ update arm set
        - **13.** for $B'\in\mathsf{child}(B)$ do
            - **14.** Set $\mathcal{I}(B')\gets\mathcal{I}(B)$. ▷ assign remaining arms in $B$ as initial arms in its children
            - **15.** Initialize the policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B')$ by Procedure 1 $\big(B',\mathcal{I}(B'),U,\mathcal{D}^{P} \big)$.
            - **16.** Set $N(B')\gets0$. ▷ initialize time for policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B')$
            - **17.** Set $\tau_{k}(B')\gets0$ and $\tau_{k}^{\star}(B';\mathcal{D}^{P})$ as in (10), $\forall k\in\mathcal{I}(B')$. ▷ initialize rounds and set round upper bounds
        - **18.** Set $\mathcal{L}_{t}\gets (\mathcal{L}_{t}\setminus B)\cup\mathsf{child}(B)$. ▷ replace $B$ with its children in partition
        - **19.** Find the bin $B\in\mathcal{L}_{t}$ such that $X_{t}^{Q}\in B$.
    - **20.** Set $N(B)\gets N(B)+1$. ▷ update times $X_{t}^{Q} \in B$
    - **21.** Set $\pi_{t}\gets\widetilde{\pi}_{N(B)}(B)$. ▷ choose arm by policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B)$
    - **22.** Set $\mathcal{I}(B)\gets\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_{N(B)} (B)$. ▷ update arm set by policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B)$
    - **23.** Set $\tau_{k}(B) \gets \widetilde{\tau}_{N(B),k}(B), \forall k\in\mathcal{I}(B)$. ▷ update numbers of rounds by policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B)$
- **24.** **Output:** policy $\{\pi_{t}\}_{t\geq1}$.

members.statement_original:
For any function $f(\cdot)$ on $\mathcal{X}$, bin $B$ in $\mathcal{X}$, and probability distribution $\lambda$ over $\mathcal{X}$, let $\Gamma_{B}f(\cdot ; \lambda)$ be the $L_{2}(\lambda)$-projection of $f$ onto the class of piecewise-constant functions over $B$, namely 
\[
\Gamma_{B}f(x ; \lambda) \coloneqq\frac{1}{\lambda(B)} \int_{B} f(u)  \, \mathsf{d}\lambda(u)\tag{15}
\]
 if $\lambda(B) > 0$, and $\Gamma_{B}f(x ; \lambda) \coloneqq 0$ otherwise.

Let $f:\mathcal{X} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be a Hölder continuous function in $\mathcal{H}(\beta, C_\beta)$ with $0<\beta \leq 1$. For any probability distribution $\lambda$ and constants $l_{0}\geq 0$, $b >0$, we say $f$ is self-similar under $\lambda$ with parameters $l_{0}$ and $b$, if the following holds for any integer $l\geq l_{0}$: 
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal{B}_{l}}\sup_{x\in B}\big|\Gamma_{B}f(x ; \lambda)-f(x)\big|\geq b2^{-\beta l}.
\]
Assume that there exists some $k\in[K]$ such that the reward function $f_{k}$ is self-similar under both $Q_{X}$ and $P_{X\,|\,\pi=k}$ with some parameters $l_{0} \geq 0$ and $b > 0$.

We denote by $\Pi(K,\beta,C_{\beta},\alpha,C_{\alpha},\underline{q},\overline{q},\gamma,c_{\gamma}, \kappa,l_{0},b)$ the class of nonparametric contextual $K$-armed bandits that satisfy Assumptions 1--4 and Definitions 1--2. Whenever clear from the context, the shorthand $\Pi(K,\beta,\alpha,\gamma, \kappa,l_{0},b)$ and $\Pi$ are used.

members.statement_original:
- **1.** **Input:** arm number $K$, horizon length $n_{Q}$, lower and upper bounds on smoothness $\underline{\beta}$ and $\overline{\beta}$, upper bound on transfer exponent $\overline{\gamma}$, $P$-data $\mathcal{D}^{P}$, tuning parameters $C_{1}, C_{2}$.
- **2.** Set $n\gets n_{P}\vee n_{Q}$.
- **3.** if $n_{P}>n_{Q}$ then
    - **4.** Set $l_{1}\gets\Big\lceil\frac{\underline{\beta}\log_{2}(n)}{(d+2\overline{\beta}+\overline{\gamma})^2}\Big\rceil$, $l_{2}\gets l_{1}+\Big\lceil\frac{1}{d}\log_{2}(\log(n))\Big\rceil$, $l_{3}\gets\Big\lceil \frac{\overline{\beta}}{\underline{\beta}}l_{1}+\frac{1}{\underline{\beta}}\log_{2}(\log(n))\Big\rceil$. ▷ bandwidths of reward function estimators
    - **5.** Set $T\gets \Big\lceil C_{1} K n^{\frac{\underline{\beta}}{d+2\overline{\beta}}}\log^{\frac{d+\overline{\gamma}}{d}}(Kn)\Big\rceil$. ▷ sample size for smoothness estimation
    - **6.** Set $\mathcal{D}_{\mathsf{se}} \gets \Big\{\big(X_{i}^{P},\pi_{i}^{P},Y_{i}^{P,(\pi_{i}^{P})}\big)\Big\}_{i=1}^{T}$, $s_{P}\gets T+1$, $s_{Q}\gets1$. ▷ samples for smoothness estimation
- **7.** else
    - **8.** Set $l_{1}\gets\Big\lceil\frac{\underline{\beta}\log_{2}(n)}{(d+2\overline{\beta})^2}\Big\rceil$, $l_{2}\gets l_{1}+\Big\lceil\frac{1}{d}\log_{2}(\log(n))\Big\rceil$, $l_{3}\gets\Big\lceil \frac{\overline{\beta}}{\underline{\beta}}l_{1}+\frac{1}{\underline{\beta}}\log_{2}(\log(n))\Big\rceil$. ▷ bandwidths of reward function estimators
    - **9.** Set $T\gets \Big\lceil C_1 n^{\frac{\underline{\beta}}{d+2\overline{\beta}}}\log(Kn)\Big\rceil$. ▷ sample size for smoothness estimation
    - **10.** for $t = 1,\dots, T$ do
        - **11.** Draw a sample $X_{t}^{Q}$, pull arm $\pi_{t}$ uniformly at random from $[K]$, and get the reward $Y_{t}^{Q,(\pi_{t})}$.
    - **12.** Set $\mathcal{D}_{\mathsf{se}} \gets \Big\{\big(X_{t}^{Q},\pi_{t},Y_{t}^{Q,(\pi_{t})}\big)\Big\}_{t=1}^{T}$, $s_{P}\gets1$, $s_{Q}\gets T+1$. ▷ samples for smoothness estimation
- **13.** Define the grid $\mathcal{M}$ 
  \[
  \mathcal{M}\coloneqq\big\{x\in\mathcal{X}:x_{i}=(k_{i}-1/2)2^{-l_{3}},\,k_{i}=[2^{l_{3}}],i=[d]\big\}.
  \]
  
- **14.** for $i\in\{1,2\},k\in[K]$ do
    - **15.** Set $\mathcal{D}_{\mathsf{se}}^{(k)} \gets \{(X_{t},Y_{t}) : (X_{t},\pi_{t},Y_{t}) \in\mathcal{D}_{\mathsf{se}}\,\, \text{ such that }\,\, \pi_{t} = k \}$.
    - **16.** for $x\in\mathcal{M}$ do
        - **17.** Find the bin $B_{i}(x)\in\mathcal{B}_{l_{i}}$ such that $x\in B_{i}(x)$.
        - **18.** Define the reward function estimator $\widehat{f}_{k}(x;2^{-l_{i}}) \coloneqq\widehat{\eta}_{k}\big(x;B_{i}(x)\big)$, where 
          \[
          \widehat{\eta}_{k}(x;B) \coloneqq\frac{\sum_{(X_{t},Y_{t})\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathsf{se}}^{(k)}}Y_{t}\mathbb{1}\{X_{t}\in B\}}
          {1 \vee \sum_{(X_{t},Y_{t})\in\mathcal{D}_{\mathsf{se}}^{(k)}}\mathbb{1}\{X_{t}\in B\}},\quad \forall B\in\mathcal{B}_{l_{i}}. 
          \tag{16}
          \]
          
- **19.** Set $\mathsf{b}\gets\max_{k\in[K]}\max_{x\in\mathcal{M}}\big|\widehat{f}_{k}(x;2^{-l_{1}})-\widehat{f}_{k}(x;2^{-l_{2}})\big|$.
- **20.** Set $\widehat{\beta}\gets-\frac{1}{l_{1}}\log(\mathsf{b})-C_{2}\frac{\log_{2}(\log (n))}{\log_{2}(n)}$.
- **21.** **Output:** smoothness estimate $(\underline{\beta}\vee\widehat{\beta})\wedge\overline{\beta}$, time steps $s_{P}$ and $s_{Q}$, policy $\{\pi_{t}\}_{1\leq t<s_{Q}}$.

members.statement_original:
Given a subset $\mathcal{D}$ of the source data $\mathcal{D}^{P}$ and the smoothness estimate $\widehat{\beta}$ returned by Procedure 2, for any non-negative integer $\tau \geq 0$, bin $B$, and arm $k$, we define 
\[
\widehat{U}_{k}(\tau,B;\mathcal{D})\coloneqq
\begin{cases}
2\sqrt{\frac{2}{\tau+n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})}\log^{+}\big(\frac{n_{Q}|B|^{d}}{\tau}\big)} \vee 2\overline{C}_{\beta}|B|^{\widehat{\beta}}, & \text{if } \tau > 0, \\
2\sqrt{\frac{2}{n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})}\log(n|B|^{d+2\widehat{\beta}})} \vee 2\overline{C}_{\beta}|B|^{\widehat{\beta}}, & \text{if } \tau = 0,
\end{cases}\tag{17}
\]
 where we recall the notations $\log^{+}(x)\coloneqq\log(x)\vee1$, $n\coloneqq n_{P}\vee n_{Q}$, and $1/0 = \infty$.

members.statement_original:
- **1.** **Input:** bin $B$, arm set $\mathcal{I}$, confidence bound function $U$, source data $\mathcal{D}$.
- **2.** Set $n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D}),\overline{Y}_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D}),\tau_{k}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D})$ as in (7), (8), (10), respectively, $\forall k\in\mathcal{I}$.
- **3.** Set $n_{k}^{P} \gets n_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})$, $\overline{Y}_{k} \gets \overline{Y}_{k}^{P}(B;\mathcal{D})$, and $\tau_{k}^{\star} \gets \tau_{k}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}), \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$.
- **4.** Initialize $t\gets0$.
- **5.** Initialize $\tau_{k} \gets 0, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$. ▷ initialize pull counts
- **6.** Initialize $\underline{Y}^{\star}\gets\max\limits_{k\in\mathcal{I}}\big\{\overline{Y}_{k}-U_{k}(0,B;\mathcal{D})\big\}$. ▷ initialize largest reward lower bound
- **7.** loop
    - **8.** if $\tau_{k}\geq\tau_{k}^{\star}, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$ then ▷ condition to stop exploration
        - **9.** Set $t \gets t+1$.
        - **10.** Select arm $\widetilde{\pi}_{t}\gets\mathop{\mathrm{argmax}}\limits_{k\in\mathcal{I}}\overline{Y}_{k}$ (with ties broken arbitrarily) and receive reward $Y^{Q,({\widetilde{\pi}_{t}})}$.
        - **11.** Set $\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\gets\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}} + 1$. ▷ update pull count
        - **12.** Set $\tau_{t,k}\gets \tau_{k}, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$, and $\mathcal{I}_{t}\gets\mathcal{I}$. ▷ record pull count and active arm set
        - **13.** Set $\overline{Y}_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\gets\frac{1}{n_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}^{P}+\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}}\big(Y^{Q,({\widetilde{\pi}_{t}})}+(n_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}^{P}+\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}-1)\overline{Y}_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\big)$. ▷ update estimated reward
    - **14.** else
        - **15.** for $k\in\mathcal{I} \text{ such that } \tau_{k}<\tau_{k}^{\star}$ do ▷ only explore arms s.t. pull counts less than upper bounds
            - **16.** if $\overline{Y}_{k}+  U_{k}(\tau_{k},B;\mathcal{D}) \geq\underline{Y}^{\star}$ then ▷ eliminate arm s.t. reward upper bound is smaller than largest reward lower bound
                - **17.** Set $t \gets t+1$.
                - **18.** Select arm $\widetilde{\pi}_{t}\gets k$ and receive reward $Y^{Q,({\widetilde{\pi}_{t}})}$.
                - **19.** Set $\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\gets\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}} + 1$. ▷ update pull count
                - **20.** Set $\tau_{t,k}\gets \tau_{k}, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}$, and $\mathcal{I}_{t}\gets\mathcal{I}$. ▷ record pull count and active arm set
                - **21.** Set $\overline{Y}_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\gets\frac{1}{n_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}^{P}+\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}}\big(Y^{Q,({\widetilde{\pi}_{t}})}+(n_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}^{P}+\tau_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}-1)\overline{Y}_{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}}\big)$. ▷ update estimated reward
                - **22.** Set $\underline{Y}^{\star}\gets\max_{k\in\mathcal{I}}\big\{\overline{Y}_{k}-U_{k}(\tau_{k},B;\mathcal{D})\big\}$. ▷ update largest reward lower bound
            - **23.** else
                - **24.** Eliminate arm $k$ from active arm set: $\mathcal{I} \gets\mathcal{I}\setminus\{k\}$.
- **25.** **Output:** policy $\{\widetilde{\pi}_{t}\}_{t\geq1}$, arm pull counts $\{(\tau_{t,k})_{k\in\mathcal{I}_t}\}_{t\geq1}$, sets of active arms $\{\mathcal{I}_{t}\}_{t\geq1}$.

invocation_context_original.text: With the smoothness estimate $\widehat{\beta}$ in hand, the second stage of Algorithm 2 takes it as an input and operates in a manner similar to Algorithm 1. We would like to highlight several pivotal differences. To begin with, as a portion of the source data may have been used in the smoothness estimation process, Algorithm 2 utilizes a subset of the source dataset $\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}}\subset \mathcal{D}^{P}$ to assist in distinguishing the optimal arm in the target bandit. Additionally, note that the confidence bound $U_{k}(\tau,B;\mathcal{D})$ (cf. (9)) used in Algorithm 1 requires the knowledge of the unknown parameters $\gamma$ and $\kappa$. To construct an adaptive procedure in Algorithm 2, we substitute it with the confidence bound $\widehat{U}_{k}(\tau,B;\mathcal{D})$ defined as follows.

The associated non-negative upper bound on play rounds is defined by 
\[
\widehat{\tau}^\star_k(B;\mathcal{D}) \coloneqq\min_{\tau \in \{0\}\cup\mathbb{N}}\big\{ \tau : \widehat{U}_{k}(\tau,B;\mathcal{D}) \leq 2\overline{C}_{\beta}|B|^{\widehat{\beta}}\big\}.\tag{18}
\]

members.statement_original:
- **1.** **Input:** arm set $\mathcal{I}$, horizon length $n_{Q}$, lower and upper bounds on smoothness $\underline{\beta}$ and $\overline{\beta}$, upper bound on Lipschitz constant $\overline{C}_\beta$, upper bound on transfer exponent $\overline{\gamma}$, $P$-data $\mathcal{D}^{P}$.
- **2.** Run Procedure 2 ($K, n_{Q}, \underline{\beta}, \overline{\beta}, \overline{\gamma}, \mathcal{D}^{P}$) to get the smoothness estimate $\widehat{\beta}$, time steps $s_{P}$ and $s_{Q}$, and policy $\{\pi_{t}^{\mathsf{a}}\}_{1\leq t <s_{Q}}$.
- **3.** Split the source data $\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}} \gets \Big\{ \big(X_{i}^{P},\pi_{i}^{P},Y^{P,(\pi_{i}^{P})} \big) \Big\}_{i=s_{P}}^{n_{P}}$ to aid in decision-making in the $Q$-bandit.
- **4.** Set $\mathcal{L}_{s_{Q}}\gets\{\mathcal{X}\}$, and $\mathcal{I}(\mathcal{X})\gets\mathcal{I}$. ▷ initialize partition and arm set
- **5.** Initialize the policy $\widetilde{\pi}(\mathcal{X})$ by Procedure 1 $\big(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{I}(\mathcal{X}), \widehat{U}, \mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}} \big)$.
- **6.** Initialize $N(\mathcal{X})\gets0$. ▷ set time to $0$ for policy $\widetilde{\pi}(\mathcal{X})$
- **7.** Initialize $\tau_{k}(\mathcal{X}) \gets 0$, and $\widehat{\tau}_{k}^{\star}(\mathcal{X};\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}})$ as in (18), $\forall k \in \mathcal{I}(\mathcal{X})$. ▷ initialize rounds and round upper bounds
- **8.** for $t=s_{Q},\dots,n_{Q}$ do
    - **9.** Draw a sample $X_{t}^{Q} \sim Q_{X}$.
    - **10.** Find the bin $B\in\mathcal{L}_{t}$ such that $X_{t}^{Q}\in B$.
    - **11.** while $|\mathcal{I}(B)|>1$ and $\tau_{k}(B)\geq\widehat{\tau}_{k}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}}), \forall k\in\mathcal{I}(B)$ do ▷ keep partitioning $B$ until reaching suitable scale
        - **12.** if $\widehat{\tau}_{k}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}}) = 0, \forall k\in\mathcal{I}(B)$ then ▷ no exploration needed in $B$: discard suboptimal arms
            - **13.** Set $\underline{Y}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}})\gets\max\limits_{k\in\mathcal{I}(B)}\big\{\overline{Y}_{k}^P(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}})-\widehat{U}_{k}(0,B;\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}})\big\}$ ▷ set largest reward lower bound
            - **14.** Set $\mathcal{I}(B) \gets \{ k \in \mathcal{I}(B) : \overline{Y}_k^P(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}}) + \widehat{U}_{k}(0,B;\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}}) \geq \underline{Y}^{\star}(B;\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}}) \}$. ▷ update arm set
        - **15.** for $B'\in\mathsf{child}(B)$ do
            - **16.** Set $\mathcal{I}(B')\gets\mathcal{I}(B)$. ▷ assign remaining arms in $B$ as initial arms in its children
            - **17.** Initialize the policy $\widetilde{\pi}({B'})$ by Procedure 1 $\big(B', \mathcal{I}(B'),\widehat{U},\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}} \big)$.
            - **18.** Set $N(B')\gets0$. ▷ initialize time for policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B')$
            - **19.** Set $\tau_{k}(B') \gets 0$, and $\widehat{\tau}_{k}^{\star}(B';\mathcal{D}^{P}_{\mathsf{dm}})$ as in (18), $\forall k\in\mathcal{I}(B')$. ▷ initialize rounds and round upper bounds
        - **20.** Set $\mathcal{L}_{t}\gets (\mathcal{L}_{t}\setminus B)\cup\mathsf{child}(B)$. ▷ replace $B$ with its children in partition
        - **21.** Find the bin $B\in\mathcal{L}_{t}$ such that $X_{t}^{Q}\in B$.
    - **22.** Set $N(B)\gets N(B)+1$. ▷ update times $X_{t}^{Q} \in B$
    - **23.** Set $\pi^{\mathsf{a}}_{t}\gets\widetilde{\pi}_{N(B)}(B)$. ▷ choose arm by policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B)$
    - **24.** Set $\mathcal{I}(B)\gets\widetilde{\mathcal{I}}_{N(B)} (B)$. ▷ update arm set by policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B)$
    - **25.** Set $\tau_{k}(B) \gets \widetilde{\tau}_{N(B),k}(B), \forall k\in\mathcal{I}(B)$. ▷ update numbers of rounds by policy $\widetilde{\pi}(B)$
- **26.** **Output:** policy $\pi^{\mathsf{a}} = \{\pi^{\mathsf{a}}_{t}\}_{t\geq1}$.
